studies.label: Experiment 1 (divergent thinking, Alternate Uses Test)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.5; PDF p. 4, Figure 2 (recruitment-to-randomization flow)

arms.name: None
arms.description: Control group. No LLM support provided. Also labeled 'No LLM Response' (Figure 2; Section 3.2).

arms.name: List of Ideas
arms.description: GPT-4o generated alternate uses for the object; seven randomly sampled uses (from a pool of 20 per object, p. 8) were shown, which participants could freely use in their responses. Figure 3 labels this panel 'LLM Answer'.

arms.name: List of Strategies
arms.description: GPT-4o with a SCAMPER system prompt (Figure 11) generated seven strategies; it guided participants without sharing explicit answers. Figure 3 labels this panel 'LLM Guidance'.

studies.task: Generate creative alternate uses for everyday objects in three exposure rounds with assigned assistance, then one unassisted test round after a one-minute Snake distractor task.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (gpt-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 16, Appendix A.1.1: model version: gpt-4o; date of use: August 2024.

preregistration.where: https://aspredicted.org/dkvp-n785.pdf (PDF p. 4, footnote 1); PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.4. Retrieval of the linked preregistration was blocked by socket permissions.
preregistration.primary_outcome: Originality of ideas in the unassisted AUT test round; the paper identifies unassisted performance as primary (Figure 1) and originality as its preregistered comparison (Section 3.1.4).

studies.label: Experiment 2 (convergent thinking, Remote Associates Test)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 4.1.5; PDF p. 9, Figure 7 (recruitment-to-randomization flow)
counts_source.quote: We recruited 640 participants from Prolific (of whom 99% passed the attention check).

arms.name: None
arms.description: Control group. Also labeled 'No LLM Response' (Figures 7, 8a) and 'No LLM Assistance' (Section 4.2.1).

arms.name: LLM Answer
arms.description: The answer generated by GPT-4o for the given set of words, shown with the compound words (Figure 8b; Table 2). The interface said participants could freely use the AI suggestion.

arms.name: LLM Guidance
arms.description: GPT-4o with a coach system prompt (Figure 12) listed five associated words for each cue word and nudged participants to jot the words down on paper. The model was instructed not to provide the solution directly (p. 9), but the words can include it: one of the three samples in Table 2 (flake, mobile, cone) lists the solution 'snow' first among the words for 'flake' (p. 18).

studies.task: Solve three Remote Associates Test problems with assigned assistance, then two unassisted problems after a one-minute Snake distractor task; each problem asks for the word linking three cues.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (gpt-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 16, Appendix B.1.1: model version: gpt-4o; date of use: August 2024.

preregistration.where: https://aspredicted.org/4q75-bskd.pdf (PDF p. 9, footnote 2); PDF p. 11, Sections 4.1.4-4.1.5. Retrieval of the linked preregistration was blocked by socket permissions.

estimates.outcome: Individual-level diversity of idea set, test round (unassisted)
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Median pairwise cosine distance between SBERT embeddings of the ideas in one participant's idea set for the test object (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3). This measures variety within a person, coded flexibility. Figure 5a displays means with error bars of one standard error of the mean; no values are printed.

sources.quote: Participants in the List of Strategies condition continued to generate more similar ideas compared to those in the No LLM Response condition (p = 0.017)
We first embed all ideas using SBERT [49]. Idea diversity is the median pairwise cosine distance between idea embeddings in the idea set.
Higher values denote more difference between ideas. Error bars represent ± one standard error of mean.

estimates.notes: The pairwise p-value is from Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction. The three-arm omnibus result is preserved in the paper-level notes. One test-round idea set per person makes the analysis participant-level. Higher distance means more variety within a participant, not diversity across people. No arm mean or numeric error-bar value was read from Figure 5. The reconciled screening form classifies this as secondary, but the linked preregistration could not be accessed and the paper does not identify its primary status separately; preregistered_primary is therefore not_stated.

estimates.outcome: RAT accuracy, test rounds (unassisted)
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Accuracy on the two unassisted RAT problems, each with one correct answer (PDF p. 9, Sections 4.1-4.1.1). Figure 9 uses percent accuracy. ANCOVA includes baseline verbal fluency as a covariate, followed by Tukey HSD comparisons (PDF p. 11, Sections 4.1.4 and 4.2.1). automated_score is the screening form's placeholder for answer-key scoring; the paper does not describe the scoring implementation.

stats.difference_is: LLM Guidance minus no LLM responses, as printed for the Tukey HSD comparison

sources.quote: LLM Guidance condition performed significantly worse than those who did not receive any LLM responses in exposure rounds (𝑝= 0.005), with a mean difference of −10.6 [95% CI: −18.6, −2.7].
a given RAT problem has a singular correct answer, we were able to define the metric for convergent thinking skills as accuracy on the RAT problems.
Figure 9: Plot of participant accuracy on the Remote Asso- ciates Task, segmented by exposure and test phase across all experimental conditions.

open_items: Neither experiment prints analyzed person counts or counts by arm. The recruited totals must not be divided among arms or converted from degrees of freedom.
For S2 the paper reports that 99% passed the attention check (PDF p. 11, Section 4.1.5), but does not state exclusions or the resulting analysis count; the percent is not an exact count.
All eligible arm means and SDs are absent. Arm levels and error bars appear only in Figures 4, 5, and 9, without numerical point labels; only Figure 5 defines its bars.

S1 originality and creative flexibility are defined per idea, but the paper does not state whether tests analyze ideas or participant means. Exposure fluency and individual diversity may use repeated participant-rounds or participant means; participant-level uncertainty is unconfirmed.

S2 test ANCOVA reports residual df of 1256 (PDF p. 11, Section 4.2.1), which exceeds the recruited person count. Answer-level analysis is inferred, but participant clustering and the exact analysis unit are not stated. No person or observation count was derived.

The S2 Tukey mean difference and confidence interval are printed without an explicit unit, adjustment description, or confirmation that the interval is simultaneous. Figure 9 displays percent accuracy. No SE or standardized effect was computed.

Group diversity uses simulated sets of ideas. The paper does not allocate the reported Monte Carlo runs to arms, items, or phases or explain how its error bars relate to independent participants. No participant-level diversity uncertainty or exact count of analyzed sets is printed.

Creative flexibility is defined using maximum cosine similarity but reported with higher values indicating greater dissimilarity. The transformation and the membership of the exposure comparison set are not specified. The embedding checkpoint and any scaling of the plotted distance measures are not reported.

The measure code automated_score for RAT accuracy is the reconciled screening form's placeholder; the codebook has no specific answer-key accuracy measure code and the paper does not describe answer scoring.
The frequency with which LLM Guidance included the correct answer is not reported; Table 2 includes an example that does.
The external preregistrations could not be retrieved in this job. Primary status beyond the main unassisted originality and accuracy analyses cannot be independently confirmed from them.
The local arXiv v2 PDF was not compared with the ACM version of record.
notes: Extracted independently as B on 2026-10-10. The complete markdown was read in sequential chunks, including references and appendices. Numerical outcome sources were checked against pymupdf PDF text; appendix tables were also checked with find_tables, and plots were inspected without digitization. The paper reports no arm means, participant SDs, numerical standard errors, or per-arm/analyzed person counts for the eligible outcomes. The recruited totals in the randomized-study flow are stored only in study n_randomized; they are not counts for any two-arm analysis. Both experiments are between-person assignments. The paper's term paired for the exposure phase refers to working with an LLM, not a randomized within-person crossover. All test-phase outputs were unassisted in the same session after a one-minute distractor task. delay_days is null because no day-based delay is printed. The standard arms receive supplied GPT-4o content, so study ai_role is ideas_supplied. List of Strategies provides SCAMPER coaching without answers; LLM Guidance supplies associated candidate words and can include the answer (the snow example in Table 2, PDF p. 18). The estimates retain the contrasts explicitly mapped in the reconciled screening form. No additional pairwise significance is inferred from an omnibus result. Pairwise Dunn and Tukey results print p-values but no numeric pairwise test statistic, so stats.test is null. Figures-only contrasts are retained with null statistics. Inventory of all printed omnibus condition results: S1 exposure originality [PDF p. 6, Section 3.2.1]: "(H(2) = 3.78, p = 0.151)."; S1 test originality [PDF p. 7, Section 3.2.1]: "(H(2) = 9.14, p = 0.010)."; S1 exposure fluency [PDF p. 7, Section 3.2.2]: "(H(2) = 8.57, p = 0.014)."; S1 test fluency [PDF p. 7, Section 3.2.2]: "(H(2) = 1.14, p = 0.566),"; S1 test creative flexibility [PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.3]: "(H(2) = 6.31, p = 0.043)."; S1 exposure individual diversity [PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.4]: "(H(2) = 9.95, p = 0.007)."; S1 test individual diversity [PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.4]: "(H(2) = 7.71, p = 0.021)."; S1 exposure group diversity, scope across all conditions; test not named in result sentence [PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.4]: "In the Exposure rounds, the average median cosine distance between ideas was similar across all conditions (p > 0.05),"; S2 test accuracy, ANCOVA condition effect [PDF p. 11, Section 4.2.1]: "main effect of condition (𝐹(2, 1256) = 5.134, 𝑝= 0.006).". These are three-arm tests or an across-condition statement, not statistics for a single two-arm contrast, and therefore are not assigned to stats.test or stats.p_value. No numerical test-phase group-diversity result or exposure RAT test is printed. Excluded covariate test [PDF p. 11, Section 4.2.1]: "performance (𝐹(1, 1256) = 16.715, 𝑝< 0.001)". PDF p. 6, Section 3.2 reports "We report on the analysis of 9,457 ideas generated by participants across all conditions and phases."; this all-phase output total is not n_units for any contrast. Printed precision, including trailing zeros in p-values, is preserved in source quotations; JSON numeric values have their ordinary serialization. The two preregistration PDFs named in the paper were attempted with urllib and the prescribed User-Agent; both were blocked by socket permissions. Their existence is confirmed by the paper, but additional primary/secondary labels from the registrations were not independently verified. No participant sharing with another paper is stated. For uncertain analysis units, the screening form's nearest unit code is retained with its qualification. The paper does not report standard errors or the analysis level for those outcomes; the available pairwise p-values are retained without claiming participant-level precision.
